The chorale and sonata scores come from Craig Sapp's Humdrum encodings, the preludes and songs from the MusicXML in *When in Rome*
(the songs from the OpenScore Lieder Corpus, their words left out), all converted to ABC here; the analyses are *When in Rome*'s. How to read
the labels and use a score: [Analysed Scores](index.qmd#reading-the-labels). A piece is left out when its score and analysis don't line
up bar for bar, or when its bars don't add up after conversion.

::: {.works-cited}
Chen, Tsung-Ping, and Li Su. *BPS-FH: Beethoven Piano Sonata with Functional Harmony* dataset (ISMIR 2018). GitHub. [github.com/Tsung-Ping/functional-harmony](https://github.com/Tsung-Ping/functional-harmony). The source of the Moonlight analysis, converted to RomanText and proof-read by Mark Gotham for When in Rome.

Digital and Cognitive Musicology Lab (DCML). *Beethoven Piano Sonatas* (harmony annotations). GitHub. [github.com/DCMLab/beethoven_piano_sonatas](https://github.com/DCMLab/beethoven_piano_sonatas). Analyses of the Beethoven movements not in the BPS dataset (CC BY-NC-SA), converted to RomanText in When in Rome.

Digital and Cognitive Musicology Lab (DCML). *The Annotated Mozart Sonatas*. GitHub. [github.com/DCMLab/mozart_piano_sonatas](https://github.com/DCMLab/mozart_piano_sonatas). The Mozart sonatas' analyses (CC BY-NC-SA), converted to RomanText in When in Rome.

Gotham, Mark, et al. *When in Rome: A Meta-Corpus of Functional Harmony*. GitHub. [github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome](https://github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome). The analyses on this page (RomanText files), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

OpenScore. *OpenScore Lieder Corpus*. GitHub. [github.com/OpenScore/Lieder](https://github.com/OpenScore/Lieder). The songs' notes (MusicXML, CC0), from which the finder's song passages are cut and the library's songs are drawn; the words are left out.

Sapp, Craig Stuart, encoder. *370 Four-part Chorales by J. S. Bach in the Humdrum File Format*. GitHub. [github.com/craigsapp/bach-370-chorales](https://github.com/craigsapp/bach-370-chorales). The chorale's notes (after Dörffel's edition, Breitkopf & Härtel, c. 1875), converted to ABC for this page.

Sapp, Craig Stuart, encoder. *Beethoven Piano Sonatas in the Humdrum File Format* (after the Durand 1915 edition, ed. Paul Dukas). GitHub. [github.com/craigsapp/beethoven-piano-sonatas](https://github.com/craigsapp/beethoven-piano-sonatas). The sonata's notes, converted to ABC for this page.

Sapp, Craig Stuart, encoder. *Mozart Piano Sonatas in the Humdrum File Format* (after the Alte Mozart-Ausgabe, vol. 20, 1878). GitHub. [github.com/craigsapp/mozart-piano-sonatas](https://github.com/craigsapp/mozart-piano-sonatas). The Mozart sonatas' notes (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), converted to ABC for the library.

Tymoczko, Dmitri, analyst. Roman-numeral analyses of the Bach chorales and of Beethoven, Piano Sonata Op. 27 No. 2, in *When in Rome*. [github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome/tree/master/Corpus](https://github.com/MarkGotham/When-in-Rome/tree/master/Corpus). The chorale's analysis; his readings of the Moonlight are quoted where they differ from Chen and Su's.
:::
